summary.text: A 60-year-old woman with no significant medical history developed loss of appetite in October 2024, then persistent fever up to 38.5°C, sore throat and a progressive malar rash. She denied arthralgia, serositis, neurologic and oral ulcer symptoms. Examination showed a well-demarcated malar rash and a tender right cervical lymph node without synovitis, edema or mucosal ulcers.

Laboratory testing showed leukopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, low C3, C4 and CH50, elevated anti-dsDNA and anti-SS-A antibodies, positive ANA and mild proteinuria without hematuria. Cervical CT showed right cervical lymph node enlargement and lymph node biopsy showed necrotizing lymphadenitis. Proteinuria rose to 0.8 g/gCr and renal biopsy showed class II lupus nephritis. SLEDAI-2K at presentation was 10.

Hydroxychloroquine 400 mg/day was started but fever, rash and cytopenias persisted. Systemic glucocorticoids were deferred with a plan to start them if HCQ proved insufficient. Anifrolumab 300 mg IV was introduced on Day 0.

Fever resolved by Day 3, leukocyte and platelet counts improved by Day 4, the rash regressed over the following weeks, and complement, anti-dsDNA antibody titers and proteinuria improved. Systemic glucocorticoids were not required and remission was achieved with HCQ and ANI alone.
